text:
maya: quick heads-up — we saw a burst that saturated model-xyz-primary in us-west-2 this morning, latency spiked to 1.2s p95 and we lost a few customer requests
rafael: saw the traces, looks like capacity queues backed up. primary had 100% queued tokens for ~3m
june: was that on Dedicated capacity or hosted?
maya: hosted for the customer, tier=pro. they were ramping a new feature 
zara: telemetry shows routing stayed pinned to primary despite health warnings from serving. metrics had a 'queue_depth' alarm but no automated failover kicked in
rafael: current rule only fails over on explicit instance health or container crash, not on capacity saturation. we omitted queue-based failover because we worried about oscillation during transient bursts
maya: customers expect graceful degradation — ideally fallback to a cheaper variant when primary is backlogged, rather than 429s
june: agree. need throttling + fallback combination: rate-limit at ingress, then if queue depth > 0.8 for >30s, route x% to variant-b1, then scale up primary
rafael: proposal draft (snip):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  on_capacity_saturation:
    threshold: 0.8
    sustained_seconds: 30
    fallback_strategy:
      type: weighted_split
      variants:
        - name: model-xyz-quant-b1
          weight: 0.7
        - name: model-xyz-8bit-b2
          weight: 0.3
    backoff_seconds: 60
```
zara: we should emit a structured event when this triggers: `fallback.invoked`, labels: tier, region, primary_qdepth, routed_variants. add a console banner so customers see automatic switch
ben: from CS side, surface in console + a notification to org admins. Also include an opt-out toggle for customers who require strict model fidelity
maya: +1 on opt-out. default behavior = auto-fallback for non-enterprise accounts, enterprise can lock to strict model pinning via new API param `model_lock: true`
june: what about rollouts UX? if we auto-fallback to quant variant we should mark experiments so evals compare output quality and alert if divergence > threshold\rafael: we can reuse the eval pipeline. when fallback active route a small mirror sample (1%) to primary for quality-checks and compute emb-duplicates to track regressions
zara: dashboards: add a panel that shows live `fallback.rate` and per-variant quality drift; also a timeline of when each fallback event happened. will need a new tag on traces `fallback=true`
maya: edge cases: what if fallback fills up too? recursion risk. we should have max_depth=1 and then a last-resort circuit-breaker returning 429 or degrade tokens
rafael: implemented as `max_fallback_hops: 1` + `circuit_breaker_threshold: 0.95` in config. also add jitter to backoff to avoid sync storms
june: operational note: need to update runbooks and oncall alerts so SREs aren't paged for expected fallback activity — maybe only page if fallback persists > 15m or quality regressions detected
devbot: deploy-bot: rolling out `auto-fallback-capacity` featureflag to staging (ff: afb-2026-capacity)
rafael: i'll draft an internal API change: POST /v1/routing/policies/{id}/fallbacks with new fields. keep backwards compat by defaulting to current behavior
maya: thanks. can we get a small PoC in staging by EOD? just the config + telemetry. no UI yet\zara: will add telemetry hooks and a staging dashboard. ping me when policy exists so I can map fields
ben: I'll prepare customer-facing note for pro accounts so they aren't surprised if we route to a slightly lower-fidelity variant
maya: ok let's sync 30 mins after deploy. if staging looks good we can soft-enable for 10% of traffic for a couple of accounts
rafael: noted. will PR config and api docs
maya: thanks team :thumbsup:
